title: WorldFoundry Unifies 270 World Models in One Benchmark
summary: WorldFoundry launches with 270 generative world models, 74 benchmarks, and 62 metrics under one open-source harness. Led by Ming-Hsuan Yang and Felix Heide.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- WorldFoundry launches as open-source infrastructure unifying 270 world models, 74 benchmarks, and 62 metrics under standardized evaluation protocols.
- Led by Ming-Hsuan Yang and Felix Heide, the framework redefines world models as persistent, history-conditioned systems beyond visual plausibility.
- Covers video, 3D, 4D, embodied action, and interactive systems with modality-specific adapters preserving native execution semantics and output representations.


A 16-author research team led by Ming-Hsuan Yang and Felix Heide has released WorldFoundry, an open-source[benchmark](https://emergent.sh/glossary/benchmark) infrastructure that standardizes inference and evaluation across 270 generative world models. Officially launched on November 10, 2026, the framework ships with 74 benchmarks and 62 registered metric entries, addressing fragmentation in how video, 3D, 4D, embodied-action, and interactive systems are assessed.


## What WorldFoundry Does


WorldFoundry defines a[world model](https://emergent.sh/glossary/world-model) as a predictive dynamical system that maintains a persistent, history-conditioned representation of an environment, updates that representation in response to actions or interventions, and generates temporally coherent trajectories. The framework moves beyond visual plausibility to enforce a functional definition spanning five intelligence-oriented layers: perceptual grounding, persistent state modeling, controllable transformation, dynamics-aware prediction, and closed-loop interaction.


Modality-specific adapters preserve native inputs, execution semantics, output representations, and evaluation protocols. This means a video diffusion model, a NeRF-based 3D generator, and an embodied-action policy can all be evaluated through the same harness without forcing them into a lowest-common-denominator format.


## Release Date and Availability


Officially released on November 10, 2026, WorldFoundry arrived on arXiv with a complete reference workflow and catalog. The initial release includes 270 model entries validated through end-to-end execution tests. Every runner in the harness has been verified for readiness, with execution evidence tracked separately from evaluative claims.


## Catalog Scope and Structure


The catalog spans five system categories:


- Video generation models
- 3D and 4D reconstruction systems
- Embodied-action policies
- Interactive simulation environments
- Hybrid multi-modal architectures


Each entry declares its inputs, state representation, forward-simulation protocol, and supported metrics. Explicit manifests and durable artifact contracts separate a model being runnable inside the harness from a model having been scored on specific benchmarks. This design prevents conflation of technical readiness with performance claims.


## Authors and Research Background


Lead author Juanxi Tian worked alongside Felix Heide and Ming-Hsuan Yang, both recognized for contributions to computer vision and generative modeling. The 16-author collaboration synthesized work from labs focused on video synthesis, robotics simulation, neural rendering, and interactive agents. The team argues that current evaluation practices privilege perceptual realism over predictive accuracy, state persistence, and action-conditioned dynamics.


## Benchmark and Metric Design


The 74 benchmarks cover tasks ranging from next-frame prediction and long-horizon rollout to closed-loop object manipulation and multi-agent coordination. The 62 registered metrics include perceptual similarity scores, physical plausibility tests, state-consistency checks, and controllability measures. Evidence-aware scorecards document which models have been executed on which benchmarks, preventing speculative comparisons.


## What This Means


WorldFoundry provides the first standardized infrastructure to compare world models across modalities and domains. By decoupling execution readiness from evaluative claims and enforcing a shared functional definition, the framework enables researchers to move beyond cherry-picked demos toward reproducible, apples-to-apples benchmarks. The project's GitHub repository and arXiv paper position it as foundational infrastructure for the next generation of generative world intelligence systems.
